clue.text: Hewas always ready to accept a new sovereign

definitions.text: Hewas always ready to accept a new sovereign

parts.words: Hewas always ready to accept a new sovereign
parts.note: describes the cleric of the old English song who kept his parish by changing allegiance under each new monarch

explanation.surface: A loyal subject happy to welcome whichever king or queen comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is an 18th-century English song about a clergyman who switched his religious and political loyalties under every ruler from Charles II to George I to keep his living.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's turncoat parson is proverbial for shifting allegiance to whoever holds the throne.

clue.text: Character missing from the Irish flag

indicators.note: missing from tells us a piece is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: the people of Ireland, the Irish
a character is a letter, here H

explanation.surface: Some symbol is absent from the flag of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is not a banner but the plant also called the yellow flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the wild yellow iris and related plants.

clue.text: Bird comes up to other birds

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: One bird approaches a flock of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds of northern seas, such as puffins and guillemots.

clue.text: They're not at home with regulations

definitions.text: They're not at home with regulations

parts.note: someone not at home is out
laws are rules or regulations

explanation.surface: Bandits are uncomfortable with rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitives from justice live beyond the law and so are no friends to rules.

clue.text: British Rail gets directions on how to make tea

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British Rail, the former UK railway operator
E, east, is a compass direction
W, west, is another compass direction

explanation.surface: The railway company issues instructions for tea-making.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'directions' supplies two compass points, E and W; 'gets' and 'on how to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew is to steep leaves in hot water to prepare a pot.

clue.text: Where you may buy duty-free wine on display

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: to air is to display or show
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Bottles of wine are laid out in a shop where tax is not charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts AIR above PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Departure lounges at an air terminal have tax-free shops for travellers.

clue.text: Band-leader waves at cus tomers

indicators.note: waves suggests the letters are swirled about into a new order

explanation.surface: A bandleader greets the clientele with a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: The band is not a musical group but a troop of boy scouts; 'waves' rearranges AT CUSTOMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult in charge of a scout troop leads that group of young people.

clue.text: Don't get confused when you notice you have a good hand

definitions.meaning: keep a clear head and perceive matters correctly

definitions.text: notice you have a good hand
definitions.meaning: in poker a straight is five cards in sequence, a strong hand

explanation.definitionFit: To think clearly is to perceive things accurately; a poker player who spots five cards in sequence has one.

clue.text: Port area

definitions.meaning: A historic harbour city in northern Israel
a unit of land measurement, 4,840 square yards

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Israeli harbour town; the other is the land measure used for fields and plots.

clue.text: Shriek at cat when upset and despondent

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of the preceding words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a cat with a shriek and then feels miserable about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the cat-owner's mood but rearranges SHRIEK AT CAT; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be heartsick is to feel deeply low and dejected.

clue.text: He may be booted on the stage

definitions.text: He may be booted on the stage

parts.words: He may be booted on the stage
parts.note: refers to the pantomime cat who famously wears boots, not to an actor being kicked off

explanation.surface: A bad actor might get kicked off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booted' suggests being thrown out; it means wearing boots, as the cat in the pantomime Puss in Boots does.
explanation.definitionFit: The booted feline hero of the pantomime is known by this pet name for a cat.

clue.text: Tied sort of worker?

parts.note: an office employee who wears a neck-tie with a shirt, not someone bound to a job

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a job they cannot leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied' suggests a worker bound to an employer, but it refers to the tie worn by office staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Office and professional staff traditionally wear a pale shirt and tie, hence the label for them.

clue.text: Neat and precise form of epitaph

indicators.note: form of suggests the letters are moulded into another shape

explanation.surface: A tidy, exact inscription on a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges NEAT and PRECISE; 'and' joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: The wish for the dead to sleep undisturbed is a common inscription on gravestones.

clue.text: One who'd change for the dance

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the words beside it

explanation.surface: Someone who would put on different clothes before going to the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' reads as changing clothes for a dance but rearranges ONE WHO'D; 'for the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American country dance or the social gathering where it is held.

clue.text: Inter alia find saltpetre

indicators.note: alia is Latin for other things, so the letters of the word before it become something else

explanation.surface: Among other things you discover potassium nitrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter alia' looks like a single Latin phrase, but 'alia' (other) rearranges INTER; 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder and curing meat, is also called nitre.

clue.text: Shemakeshatsmoredecorative yetneater

definitions.meaning: she makes hats more decorative: someone who adds ribbons and feathers to hats
yet neater: more tidy and orderly, with yet as a link

explanation.walkthrough: The scan runs the words together: read 'She makes hats more decorative yet neater', with 'yet' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner who adds ribbons to hats is one who trims; as an adjective it is the comparative of trim, meaning tidier.

clue.text: Heath Robinson's heart beat

indicators.note: heart points to letters taken from inside the words named before it

explanation.surface: The cartoonist Heath Robinson's heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famed for absurdly elaborate contraptions; the letters run across the join of his names.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, as of the heart.

clue.text: It's to be seen on a rifle

definitions.text: It's to be seen on a rifle

parts.words: It's to be seen on a rifle
parts.note: plays on the device for aiming a gun and the general sense of something seen

explanation.surface: Something visible on the barrel of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works both ways: the aiming device fixed to a gun, and the word for anything that can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle carries an aiming device of this name, and the same word means a thing seen.

clue.text: Drinks to the return of a good man

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the return of tells us the piece after it is read backwards

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good man

explanation.surface: A toast raised to welcome back a fine fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'good man' as the definition with a hidden reversal, which defines nothing; 'Drinks' is the definition, and 'the return of' turns ST into TS after TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tots are small measures of spirits, such as whisky.

clue.text: A way one takes wine

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone takes a glass of wine in a particular manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white Italian wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Former churchman?

definitions.meaning: the deputy head of an abbey or head of a priory

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means earlier; as a noun it is a monastic officer ranking below an abbot.

clue.text: Locate unpleasant smell, but this won't cure it

parts.note: to place is to locate or identify
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Find the source of a bad smell, though this remedy will not cure it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill has no medical effect and works, if at all, only through belief.

clue.text: Refreshed sheep tear about

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to rend is to tear
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A revived sheep rips at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REND around EWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something renewed has been restored or made fresh again.

clue.text: Sympathise with number drawing unemployment benefit

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
in Britain someone claiming jobless benefit is said to be on the dole

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry for someone who is out of work and claiming benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the dole' is British slang for receiving state unemployment money.
explanation.definitionFit: To condole with someone is to express sorrow and fellow feeling for them.

clue.text: Beg for quarter in the wood

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: beech is a kind of tree and its timber
SE, south-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Pleading for mercy while hiding in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' suggests mercy, fitting 'Beg for'; it is the compass point SE placed inside BEECH. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or plead earnestly.

clue.text: Right out of line

indicators.note: out of here means the letters of the word that follows are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Something correct has gone wrong and strayed out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim over property held until a debt is paid.

clue.text: A girl raised a cry of woe

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman lets out a wail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses SAL to LAS in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection expressing grief or regret.

clue.text: A drop in rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye when crying
a rip or split in fabric

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a single drop shed when weeping and a rip in cloth, two senses pronounced differently.

clue.text: Labour staged a walk-out?

explanation.definitionFit: Britain's Labour Party belongs to the political wing opposite the right; strikers who walked out departed.

clue.text: Tropical disease that may make one feel very low

indicators.note: may make suggests the following letters can be reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: An illness from hot climates that leaves sufferers miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges FEEL VERY LOW; 'that' and 'one' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A viral infection spread by mosquitoes in hot regions, named for the jaundice it causes.

clue.text: A way through on foot

parts.note: suggests a pedestrian path but combines an ... and the curved part of the sole

explanation.surface: A path you can walk along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A way through' is an archway, and the foot has its own curved part of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: An archway is a passage under a curved structure, and the foot's raised curve shares the name.

clue.text: Thoughtful enough to study the team and make an assessment

parts.note: to con is to study or learn carefully
a side is a sports team
to rate is to judge or evaluate

explanation.surface: A coach is kind enough to look over the players and give feedback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enough to' and 'and' are links joining the three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone considerate shows kindly regard for the feelings of others.
